The '''International Centre for Sports Studies''', commonly known as the '''CIES''' ([[French language|French]]: '''''Centre International d'Etude du Sport)''''', is an independent research and education centre located in [[Neuchâtel]], Switzerland. It has a research group named the '''CIES Football Observatory''' that studies and researches the [[statistics]] of [[association football|football]].<ref name=about>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-observatory.com/-About-|title=About|department=Football Observatory|publisher= International Centre for Sports Studies|access-date=25 May 2019}}</ref>

==Origin==
CIES was created in 1995 as a [[joint venture]] between [[Fédération Internationale de Football Association|FIFA]], the [[University of Neuchâtel]], and the City and State of Neuchâtel.

==Research==
CIES Football Observatory mostly conducts research on the transfer values of players<ref>"[https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/43373081 Mohamed Salah: Liverpool forward's transfer value rises most in Europe]", ''[[BBC Sport]]'', 12 March 2018</ref><ref>"[https://www.espn.com/soccer/club/real-madrid/86/blog/post/3343674/why-is-cristiano-ronaldo-only-49th-most-valuable-cies-explains Why is Cristiano Ronaldo only 49th most valuable?]", ''[[ESPN]]'', 10 January 2018</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-observatory.com/IMG/pdf/note01en.pdf|title=Scientific assessment of football players' transfer value|department=Football Observatory|publisher=International Centre for Sports Studies (CIES)|date=October 2018|access-date=25 May 2019|first1=Raffaele|last1=Poli|first2=Loïc|last2=Ravenel|first3=Roger|last3=Besson|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170908153234/http://www.football-observatory.com/IMG/pdf/note01en.pdf|archive-date=8 September 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> and team profiles.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.foxsports.ph/football/665103/just-how-equal-are-southeast-asian-leagues/|title=Just how equal are Southeast Asian leagues?|date=17 April 2017|access-date=25 May 2019|work=Fox Sports|archive-date=25 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190525155137/https://www.foxsports.ph/football/665103/just-how-equal-are-southeast-asian-leagues/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|url=https://resources.fifa.com/mm/document/tournament/competition/02/92/14/30/ciesstudy_neutral.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171215054141/http://resources.fifa.com/mm/document/tournament/competition/02/92/14/30/ciesstudy_neutral.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 15, 2017|title=2018 FIFA World Cup: profile of qualified teams|access-date=25 May 2019|first1=Raffaele|last1=Poli|first2=Loïc|last2=Ravenel|first3=Roger|last3=Besson|journal=CIES Football Observatory Monthly Report|date=December 2017|issue=30|via=FIFA.com}}</ref>

CIES organizes and offers a one-year postgraduate sports executive program, endorsed by FIFA,<ref>[https://www.fifama.org/sites/default/files/2015%20postgraduate%20sports%20course%20rankings.pdf SportBusiness International 2015 Postgraduate Sports Course Rankings] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160527114140/https://www.fifama.org/sites/default/files/2015%20postgraduate%20sports%20course%20rankings.pdf |date=27 May 2016 }}</ref> which consists of three modules that are taught across three universities in Europe, and concludes with a final project.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cies.ch/en/education/fifa-master/about-fifa-master/about-fifa-master/|title=About FIFA Master|publisher=CIES|access-date=10 August 2013}}</ref> The successful conclusion of the program merits the award of '''FIFA Master''' International in Management, Law and Humanities of Sport.<ref>"[https://www.masterstudies.com/universities/Switzerland/CIES-International-Centre-for-Sports-Studies/ CIES]", Master Studies website, 2018</ref> It was created in 2000 to promote a managerial culture within the sports industry, with the aim to develop the skills of aspiring managers so that they can take on the complex challenges of this industry.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cies.ch/en/education/fifa-master/about-fifa-master/background/|title=Background|publisher=CIES|access-date=10 August 2013}}</ref>

With around 20 nationalities represented in class each year, the FIFA Master provides an international and dynamic learning environment, and focuses on three major and interconnected subject fields: management (SDA Bocconi), law (Neuchâtel) and human sciences (De Montfort). The strengths of the FIFA Master in the key areas of graduate employability, alumni networks, quality of teaching and international appeal has seen the programme named as the top postgraduate sports management course in the world by SportBusiness International in their 2014 rankings. Established in 2000, the FIFA Master scooped the top global award at this year's ceremony, having previously been named as the leading course in Europe by the same rankings from 2012 to 2015. More than 500 international sport management courses and alumni submitted data to the 2014 rankings process.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cies.ch/en/cies/news/news/article/fifa-master-award-no-1-in-the-world/|title=FIFA Master Award No 1 in the World|publisher=FIFA|access-date=21 May 2014}}</ref>

The Master offers students the chance to meet with top international managers from the world of sport (e.g. clubs, federations, associations, etc.) and to be part of a network of highly relevant contacts. Graduates from the course become members of the FMA (the FIFA Master Alumni Association), which guarantees they will remain in touch with important  stakeholders in sport.

===De Montfort University===
Humanities of Sport – The first term is taught at the International Centre for Sport History and Culture (ICSHC) at the De Montfort University, Leicester. The ICSHC was established in 1996 and is today widely acknowledged as the leading centre for the study of sports history in the world. The Humanities of Sport modules addresses the birth of modern sport, professionalisation and internationalisation of sport and sport ethics.

===SDA Bocconi===
Sport Management – The second term is taught at the SDA Bocconi School of Management, Milan, one of Europe's most prestigious business schools. This term addresses the area of Sports Management and covers topics such as finance, marketing, organization and governance, strategy, business planning, and event management, applied to the context of sport.

===Université de Neuchâtel===
Sport Law – The third and final term is taught at the Université de Neuchâtel, Neuchâtel, whose Law Faculty is one of the top law faculties in Switzerland. This term addresses the area of Sports Law and covers topics such as the legal aspects of the private sector of sport, the legal status of the sports person, legal aspects of sport and health, sport business and law, and methods of dispute resolution.

===Final project===
The Final Project of the FIFA Master in Management, Law, & Humanities of Sport is seen as an opportunity for postgraduates to conduct original research, demonstrate creativity and independent thinking, as well as to develop and defend their ideas. Working in small research teams, postgraduates develop an inter-disciplinary research project with reference to the course themes of Management, Law and the Humanities of Sport. The final work, which is expected to have an applicable nature to issues faced in world sport, is presented to a specially invited audience of industry and academic experts during a special conference event in Neuchâtel. Previous Final Projects have been implemented directly by sports organizations or by course Alumni in the sports industry.

CIES' postgraduates are examined throughout the FIFA Master in Management, Law, & Humanities of Sport by a variety of assessment methods. These include group assessments, written examinations, oral examinations and research papers. The assessment timetable is devised by each of the three partner universities.
